findings.where: End of the content, the coral 'Browse destinations' button (desktop-02 and phone-02)
findings.fault: The button has fully rounded pill ends. The rules file sets the primary button's corner at the 8px control radius and keeps pill corners for badges, tags and status chips. The site's one main call to action is therefore shaped like a badge, not like its other buttons.
findings.who_objects: The brand owner, because DESIGN.md sets the primary button's shape and this page breaks it. A visitor who moves on to the search and home pages would see their coral button with square-ish corners, so the same action would look different from page to page.

findings.where: First screen on desktop, the turquoise 'No hostel can pay for a higher position.' block against the reading column below it (desktop-01)
findings.fault: The turquoise block runs about 120px wider than the text column under it. Its right edge stops at about 834px, while the lede, list and method paragraphs stop at about 715px. The page's only coloured shape therefore lines up with nothing else on the page. On phone the two edges match, which makes the desktop mismatch look accidental.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to trust the ranking. This page asks to be read as careful and exact, and a hero block that overhangs the column it introduces looks like a layout slip.
